title: Real-World Production Incident Post-Mortem & Architecture Debrief

sections.title: 1. Production Scenario & Infrastructure Goal
sections.content: A high-growth SaaS enterprise with 96-core bare-metal servers required a production-grade infrastructure modernization. The goal was to establish a zero-Kubernetes reproducible local development workflow for developers, a change-aware Jenkins CI pipeline, and an automated GitOps continuous deployment pipeline via ArgoCD, Harbor, and HashiCorp Vault.

sections.title: 2. Local Dev Architecture (Makefile + Docker Compose)
sections.content:
Instead of forcing developers to run heavy Kubernetes clusters locally, we instituted the **Local Dev Contract**:
- **Single Entrypoint**: `make dev` builds multi-stage local Docker images (`Dockerfile.local`) and launches microservices in Docker Compose.
- **Secret Isolation**: `secrets.template.yaml` is committed with fake placeholders. Developers copy it to `secrets.yaml` which is strictly gitignored.
- **No Local Overhead**: Vault, cert-manager, and ArgoCD are bypassed locally to ensure developers can spin up the stack in under 60 seconds.

sections.title: 3. Change-Aware CI/CD Architecture (Jenkins + ArgoCD)
sections.content:
To prevent slow 40-minute builds on every commit, we built a **Change-Aware CI Pipeline**:
- **Path Detection**: Jenkins compares `git diff` against `develop`/`main` to flag changed services.
- **Global Safety Gates**: Runs secret leak scanning and Cargo vulnerability audits regardless of changed paths.
- **GitOps CD Rollouts**: On release tags (`v1.2.0`), images are pushed to Harbor, Kustomize overlay image tags are updated, and ArgoCD automatically reconciles K8s clusters with self-healing and zero-downtime rolling updates.

sections.title: 4. Incident Post-Mortem: Stuck Init:1/2 & NetworkPolicy Debugging
sections.content:
During production rollout, `encryption-server` pods were stuck at `Init:1/2` waiting for Redis connectivity.
- **Diagnosis**: DNS resolved `redis-service` correctly, but NetworkPolicy silently dropped traffic.
- **Root Cause**: `NetworkPolicy` used `name: encryption` instead of K8s standard `kubernetes.io/metadata.name: encryption`.
- **Fix**: Updated `namespaceSelector` label matching and added HTTP `/health` readiness probes (`initialDelaySeconds: 20`, `periodSeconds: 5`) to ensure pods pass health checks before ArgoCD marks deployments as `Healthy`.
